resources.string: Curfew
Curfew site blocking

Curfew reads the name of the app in the foreground so it can replace the ones you have chosen to block. To block websites it also reads the address bar of a browser it recognises. While a lock is running it checks whether the screen in front is the Curfew settings or uninstall page, so it can hold that page shut; that check looks only for its own name. It never reads payment, banking or password apps. Nothing it sees is stored, and nothing leaves your device. Because this service can read a screen, some banking and payment apps will refuse to run while it is on; Curfew\'s app-only service cannot read a screen and costs nothing elsewhere.
Curfew app blocking

Curfew reads the name of the app in the foreground so it can replace the ones you have chosen to block. That is all it can see: this service cannot read the contents of any screen, so it cannot block websites and cannot guard against Curfew being uninstalled. It also cannot be objected to by banking and payment apps, which is exactly why it exists. Nothing it sees is stored, and nothing leaves your device.

Precise blocking
Curfew needs to see which app is in front to replace it the moment it opens.

Without it Curfew falls back to the system\'s usage log, which does work — but it notices an app up to a second or two late, cannot re-assert a block, and cannot block a website. Turning this on makes blocking precise. There are two versions of the service and the choice is yours: app blocking alone reads no screen, so nothing outside Curfew notices it; app and site blocking also reads a browser\'s address bar to block sites and to guard against Curfew being uninstalled, and some banking and payment apps will refuse to run while it is on. Whichever you pick, you can block any app you like, and Curfew never reads the screen of a payment, banking or password app.
App blocking, precise
App and site blocking
Blocks any app the moment it opens, reads no screen. No site rules, and no uninstall guard.
Blocks any app the moment it opens, and reads a browser\'s address bar to block sites. Some banking and payment apps will refuse to run.
Every version blocks apps; the fallback needs no special access at all. What changes is how quickly a block lands, and whether Curfew may read a browser\'s address bar.
The other accessibility service is also switched on, which keeps the banking-app warning without adding anything. Turn off %1$s to get the benefit of this mode.

Usage access
Two things: time budgets are counted from the system\'s own usage figures, and if you do not grant Precise blocking, this is what tells Curfew which app is in front.
Budgets and launch limits stop counting. Without Precise blocking as well, nothing can be blocked either — this is the only detector left.
Display over other apps
Some launchers refuse to show the block screen from the background without it.
A blocked app may flash into view for a moment before it is replaced.
Notifications
The ongoing notification is how you can always tell that enforcement is running.
Enforcement still runs, but Android may show its own generic notice instead.
Exact alarms
A session that should start at 09:00 has to start at 09:00, not whenever the system next wakes.
Sessions can start up to a few minutes late.
Calendar
Calendar rules read event titles to decide when a profile should run.
Calendar rules never match; weekly schedules are unaffected.
Notification access
Silencing an app\'s notifications is the one thing Android will not let Curfew do without it.
Rules that mute notifications do nothing; everything else is unaffected. Granting it lets Curfew see every notification on the device, so leave it off unless you use a mute rule.
Unrestricted battery use
Aggressive battery savers kill background services, and a blocker that is killed blocks nothing.
Curfew may be stopped by the system and stop enforcing without warning.
Uninstall protection (device admin)

Android will not uninstall an app that is an active device admin, which closes the last easy way out of a running lock. Curfew already holds its own settings and uninstall pages shut through the accessibility service; this is the stricter version of the same idea.

Nothing inside Curfew changes: every block, schedule and lock works the same either way. The cost is outside it — many banking and payment apps refuse to run while any device admin is active, so leave this off if you use one. Curfew asks for no admin powers beyond being active: it cannot erase, lock or unlock the device, or touch any password, and you can turn it off whenever no lock is running.

resources.string: Apps Curfew never reads

Curfew does not read the screen of a payment, banking, wallet or password app. The accessibility privilege is broad and a bank\'s screen is none of its business, so those screens are skipped before anything else happens. They can still be blocked like any other app — blocking one costs a block screen and nothing else, because its notifications are never suppressed.
Covered by the shipped list
